By Alice Atkins and Michael MacKenzieOctober 29, 2026 at 2:07 PM UTCBookmark

Bank of America Corp.’s macro traders are limiting risk exposure heading into year-end after upheaval in some of the world’s most popular trades.
Swings in European interest rates have been particularly vexing for macro funds this year, according to Carlos Fernandez-Aller, co-head of global fixed income, currencies and commodities macro trading at the bank. While emerging-market investors have generally performed better, the deep Brazilian selloff that followed President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s surprise victory has jolted that sector, too, and highlighted how easily rallies can reverse.

Reaching 2% Inflation Will Be Challenging for the Fed, Feroli Says

Feroli says he was surprised that Fed Governor Lisa Cook called on the FOMC to raise rates by a quarter percentage point. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance."

A global rally in technology shares faltered as disappointing earnings from two industry heavyweights revived doubts over whether billions of dollars in artificial-intelligence spending will deliver sufficient returns.
The Nasdaq 100 fell about 1.5%. Google’s parent Alphabet Inc. sank a record 13% on a sales miss. Samsung Electronics Co. boosted AI spending, but failed to outline plans to share ballooning profits. Microsoft Corp. is looking to raise at least $25 billion from a US investment-grade bond sale. Amazon.com Inc. and Intel Corp. will report results after the closing bell.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Blistering cloud growth sent Amazon.com Inc. shares soaring after its last earnings report. Now with more than half those gains gone, the firm needs to deliver a repeat performance in order to reignite its faltering stock.
The stock had its best day since 2012 on July 31 after the e-commerce and cloud giant’s second-quarter results showed that revenue at Amazon Web Services, its cloud business, was accelerating faster than Wall Street expected. But the shares have struggled since then, down more than 10% from an early August record, as jitters about the AI trade, pressure from higher interest rates and competition from AI services such as Meta Platforms Inc.’s Muse cut into market sentiment.

Save
Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Poundland Group Ltd began insolvency proceedings just over a year after the discount retailer was bought by Gordon Brothers for £1 ($1.38), in another blow to Britain’s ailing high streets.
The move on Thursday to file a court notice of its intention to go into administration puts about 12,000 jobs at risk across roughly 600 stores. The distressed investment firm closed some stores after taking over last June but has in recent months struggled to offload the high street staple.
